GEOGRAPHY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: GEOGRAPHY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which statement about Statistical Methods is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Statistical Methods with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Say Statistical Methods never happens in Kenya.
   C. Skip evidence when discussing Statistical Methods.
   D. Treat Statistical Methods as rumours only.

2. Which statement about Weathering is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Weathering as rumours only.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Weathering.
   C. Say Weathering never happens in Kenya.
   D. Explain Weathering with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

3. Which statement about Vegetation is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Vegetation.
   B. Explain Vegetation with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Say Vegetation never happens in Kenya.
   D. Treat Vegetation as rumours only.

4. Which statement about Mass Wasting is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Mass Wasting as rumours only.
   B. Say Mass Wasting never happens in Kenya.
   C. Skip evidence when discussing Mass Wasting.
   D. Explain Mass Wasting with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

5. Citizenship responsibility includes: (1 mark)
   A. Littering in markets
   B. Destroying road signs
   C. Avoiding all community work
   D. Obeying laws and caring for public property

6. Which statement about Soils is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Soils as rumours only.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Soils.
   C. Say Soils never happens in Kenya.
   D. Explain Soils with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

7. Kenya’s capital city is: (1 mark)
   A. Kisumu
   B. Nairobi
   C. Mombasa
   D. Nakuru

8. Which statement about Weather is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Weather with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Say Weather never happens in Kenya.
   C. Skip evidence when discussing Weather.
   D. Treat Weather as rumours only.

9. Which statement about Climate is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Climate never happens in Kenya.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Climate.
   C. Treat Climate as rumours only.
   D. Explain Climate with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

10. A budget helps a family to: (1 mark)
   A. Avoid saving forever
   B. Hide all money underground
   C. Ignore prices in shops
   D. Plan income and spending wisely

11. Which statement about Geographic Information Systems is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Geographic Information Systems as rumours only.
   B. Explain Geographic Information Systems with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Skip evidence when discussing Geographic Information Systems.
   D. Say Geographic Information Systems never happens in Kenya.

12. Which statement about Agriculture - Wheat in Kenya and Russia - Maize in Kenya and Mexico, - Coffee in is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Agriculture - Wheat in Kenya and Russia - Maize in Kenya and Mexico, - Coffee in.
   B. Explain Agriculture - Wheat in Kenya and Russia - Maize in Kenya and Mexico, - Coffee in with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Treat Agriculture - Wheat in Kenya and Russia - Maize in Kenya and Mexico, - Coffee in as rumours only.
   D. Say Agriculture - Wheat in Kenya and Russia - Maize in Kenya and Mexico, - Coffee in never happens in Kenya.

13. A map key (legend) is used to: (1 mark)
   A. Replace the compass rose
   B. Measure rainfall only
   C. Name the president
   D. Explain symbols used on a map

14. Which statement about Map Reading and Interpretation is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Map Reading and Interpretation.
   B. Explain Map Reading and Interpretation with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Treat Map Reading and Interpretation as rumours only.
   D. Say Map Reading and Interpretation never happens in Kenya.

15. Which statement about Elementary Surveying is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Elementary Surveying never happens in Kenya.
   B. Treat Elementary Surveying as rumours only.
   C. Explain Elementary Surveying with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Elementary Surveying.

16. Which statement about Water Cycle and Action of Rivers is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Water Cycle and Action of Rivers never happens in Kenya.
   B. Treat Water Cycle and Action of Rivers as rumours only.
   C. Explain Water Cycle and Action of Rivers with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Water Cycle and Action of Rivers.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Map Reading and Interpretation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Elementary Surveying and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Statistical Methods and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Geographic Information Systems and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Weather and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Climate and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Vegetation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Weathering and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Mass Wasting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Soils and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
